exercises.name: Back Squat

equipment.raw: Barbell, squat rack, plates. *Swaps*: front squat · goblet squat · safety bar squat · belt squat

form_cues: Sit between your hips, not behind them
Hit depth, drive through full foot
common_errors: Heels lifting at depth (ankle mobility limit)
Excessive forward lean (often a quad-strength or ankle issue)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with hamstring-dominant work (RDL, hamstring curl), upper-body push or pull, core anti-rotation. Poor pair with heavy front squat or deadlift in same session (CNS conflict).
sources: Schoenfeld, B. (2010). Squatting kinematics and kinetics and their application to exercise performance. J Strength Cond Res.
Hartmann, H. et al. (2013). Influence of squatting depth on jumping performance. J Strength Cond Res.
Rippetoe, M. Starting Strength (3rd ed., Aasgaard, 2011).

exercises.name: Front Squat

equipment.raw: Barbell, squat rack, plates. *Swaps*: goblet squat · zercher squat · safety bar squat

exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with hamstring/glute work (RDL, hip thrust), upper-body work. Poor pair with overhead pressing same session (rack-position fatigue compounds).
sources: Gullett, J. et al. (2009). A biomechanical comparison of back and front squats in healthy trained individuals. J Strength Cond Res.
Yavuz, H. et al. (2015). Kinematic and EMG activities during front and back squat variations in maximum loads. J Sports Sci.

exercises.name: Overhead Squat

equipment.raw: Barbell, plates. Optional rack. *Swaps*: dumbbell overhead squat · single-arm overhead squat · front squat (when overhead is contraindicated)

exercises.pairing_logic: Useful as warm-up or low-load skill work. Poor as fatigued accessory (form degrades fast).
sources: Donnelly, D. et al. (2006). The effect of overhead squat performance on vertical jump performance. J Strength Cond Res.
Lorenzetti, S. et al. (2018). Comparison of the angles and corresponding moments in the knee and hip during restricted and unrestricted squats. BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil.

exercises.name: Box Squat

equipment.raw: Barbell, squat rack, plates, plyo box or bench at squat depth. *Swaps*: pause squat (no box) · pin squat (rack pins at depth)

form_cues: Sit back to box (don't squat down to it)
exercises.pairing_logic: Excellent paired with hamstring/posterior work. Pairs with upper body work. Less ideal stacked with heavy back squats.
sources: McBride, J. et al. (2010). Comparison of kinetic variables and muscle activity during a squat vs. a box squat. J Strength Cond Res.
Tate, D. Westside Barbell Book of Methods (Westside Barbell, 2008).

exercises.name: Conventional Deadlift

equipment.raw: Barbell, plates (preferably bumper or competition-style for full ROM). *Swaps*: trap bar deadlift · sumo deadlift · Romanian deadlift

form_cues: Shoulders slightly ahead of bar at start
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with upper-body push/pull (different system). Poor pair with heavy squat same session (CNS + low back fatigue). Poor finisher (form fades under fatigue).
sources: Escamilla, R. et al. (2000). A three-dimensional biomechanical analysis of sumo and conventional style deadlifts. Med Sci Sports Exerc.
Hales, M. (2010). Improving the deadlift: understanding biomechanical constraints and physiological adaptations to resistance exercise. Strength Cond J.
Rippetoe, M. Starting Strength (3rd ed., 2011).

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift

equipment.raw: Barbell, plates. *Swaps*: conventional deadlift · trap bar deadlift · wide-stance Romanian deadlift

form_cues: Push knees out as you set up
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with upper body and core. Poor stacked with conventional deadlift. Poor as finisher.
sources: Escamilla, R. et al. (2000). A three-dimensional biomechanical analysis of sumo and conventional style deadlifts. Med Sci Sports Exerc.
Belcher, D. (2017). The sumo deadlift. Strength Cond J.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift (RDL)

equipment.raw: Barbell, plates. *Swaps*: dumbbell RDL · kettlebell RDL · single-leg RDL · cable RDL

form_cues: Soft knees, don't bend more than start position
Stand tall, squeeze glutes at top
common_errors: Squatting the movement (knees bend too much)
exercises.pairing_logic: Excellent in supersets with quad-dominant or upper body. Pairs with hip thrust as posterior chain duo. Poor finisher after heavy deadlift (overlapping stimulus).
sources: McAllister, M. et al. (2014). Muscle activation during various hamstring exercises. J Strength Cond Res.
Schoenfeld, B. Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy (Human Kinetics, 2nd ed. 2020).
Helms, Morgan, Valdez. The Muscle and Strength Pyramid: Training (2nd ed., 2019).

exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift

equipment.raw: Trap bar (hex bar), plates. *Swaps*: conventional deadlift · sumo deadlift · dumbbell deadlift

form_cues: Stand inside the trap bar, mid-foot under handles
common_errors: Squatting too low at setup (becomes pure squat)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs well with most accessories given lower spinal load than conventional. Suitable as primary in general strength programs.
sources: Camara, K. et al. (2016). An examination of muscle activation and power characteristics while performing the deadlift exercise with straight and hexagonal barbells. J Strength Cond Res.
Swinton, P. et al. (2011). A biomechanical analysis of straight and hexagonal barbell deadlifts using submaximal loads. J Strength Cond Res.

exercises.name: Bench Press

equipment.raw: Barbell, bench, rack. *Swaps*: dumbbell bench press · machine chest press · push-up (for scaling) · floor press

form_cues: Bar to lower chest, slight angle
Drive feet into floor as you press
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with rowing variations (antagonist superset) or lower-body work. Poor stacked with heavy overhead pressing same session (shoulder fatigue).
sources: Krzysztofik, M. et al. (2020). The effects of resistance training experience on the bench press throw. Int J Environ Res Public Health.
Madsen, N., McLaughlin, T. (1984). Kinematic factors influencing performance and injury risk in the bench press exercise. Med Sci Sports Exerc.
Rippetoe, M. Starting Strength (3rd ed., 2011).

exercises.name: Incline Bench Press

equipment.raw: Barbell, incline bench (~30°), rack. *Swaps*: incline dumbbell press · landmine press · low-incline machine press

form_cues: Set bench to ~30° (steeper shifts to shoulders)
Drive bar slightly back, not straight up
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with row variations. Pairs with arm/shoulder isolation work. Pairs less well with overhead press same session.
sources: Trebs, A. et al. (2010). An electromyographic analysis of 3 muscles surrounding the shoulder joint during the performance of a chest press exercise at several angles. J Strength Cond Res.
Lauver, J. et al. (2017). Influence of bench angle on upper extremity muscular activation during bench press exercise. Eur J Sport Sci.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Bench Press

equipment.raw: Barbell, bench, rack. *Swaps*: close-grip dumbbell press · diamond push-up · dip · floor press close grip

form_cues: Grip slightly inside shoulder width (not painfully narrow)
common_errors: Bar path too high on chest
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with rowing or pulling work. Pairs with overhead triceps extension as triceps duo. Less ideal stacked with heavy regular bench.
sources: Lehman, G. (2005). The influence of grip width and forearm pronation/supination on upper-body myoelectric activity during the flat bench press. J Strength Cond Res.
Saeterbakken, A. et al. (2017). Effects of bench press with and without weight chains on velocity and power output. J Strength Cond Res.

exercises.name: Overhead Press (Standing Barbell)

equipment.raw: Barbell, plates, rack. *Swaps*: standing dumbbell press · seated barbell press · seated dumbbell press · landmine press · machine shoulder press

form_cues: Bar in front of shoulders at start, elbows slightly forward
Drive head through arms at lockout
common_errors: Excessive lower back arch (becomes incline press standing)
Pressing bar around face instead of past
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with rowing or pulling. Poor stacked with heavy bench same session (shoulder fatigue). Poor as finisher (form degrades).
sources: Saeterbakken, A., Fimland, M. (2013). Effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses. J Strength Cond Res.
Lauver, J. et al. (2017). Influence of bench angle on upper extremity muscular activation during bench press exercise. Eur J Sport Sci.
Rippetoe, M. Starting Strength (3rd ed., 2011).

exercises.name: Push Press

equipment.raw: Barbell, plates, rack. *Swaps*: dumbbell push press · single-arm push press · jerk (more advanced)

substitution_alternatives.name: standing barbell press (without leg drive, scaled load)

exercises.primary_muscles: Anterior deltoid · Lateral deltoid · Triceps · Quadriceps (drive)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with pulling work. Pairs with hybrid conditioning work. Poor stacked with heavy strict overhead press.
sources: Lake, J. et al. (2014). The effect of push press load on kinetic and kinematic indicators of lower body power. J Strength Cond Res.
Cormie, P. et al. (2007). The influence of body mass on calculation of power during lower-body resistance exercises. J Strength Cond Res.

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Bent-Over Row)
exercises.unilateral_note: (single-arm DB row is the unilateral variant)

equipment.raw: Barbell, plates. *Swaps*: dumbbell row · pendlay row · t-bar row · seal row · chest-supported row

exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with bench press as antagonist superset. Pairs with vertical pull (different angle). Pairs less well stacked with heavy deadlifts (low back fatigue).
sources: Fenwick, C. et al. (2009). Comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load, and stiffness. J Strength Cond Res.
Lehman, G. et al. (2004). The importance of normalisation in the interpretation of surface electromyography. J Manipulative Physiol Ther.

exercises.name: Pendlay Row

equipment.raw: Barbell, plates. *Swaps*: barbell row (continuous) · t-bar row · chest-supported row

form_cues: Bar starts on floor each rep
common_errors: Not resetting on floor (becomes barbell row)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with horizontal push and core work. Poor stacked with deadlifts (low back). Works well in strength-endurance circuits.
sources: Fenwick, C. et al. (2009). Comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load, and stiffness. J Strength Cond Res.
Schoenfeld, B. (2010). Squatting kinematics and kinetics and their application to exercise performance. J Strength Cond Res.

exercises.name: T-Bar Row

equipment.raw: T-bar row machine or barbell + landmine attachment + V-handle. *Swaps*: barbell row · chest-supported row · seal row · Cluster 3 #55 Cable Row

form_cues: Hinge at hips, slight knee bend
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with horizontal push. Pairs with arm/biceps work. Less ideal stacked with deadlifts.
sources: Fenwick, C. et al. (2009). Comparison of different rowing exercises. J Strength Cond Res.
Schoenfeld, B. Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy (Human Kinetics, 2nd ed. 2020).

exercises.name: Pull-up

equipment.raw: Pull-up bar. *Swaps*: assisted pull-up (band, machine, or partner) · Cluster 3 #54 Lat Pulldown · inverted row (for scaling)

form_cues: Hang with shoulders engaged (don't dead-hang slack)
common_errors: Craning neck instead of pulling chest up
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs excellently with overhead press as antagonist. Pairs with dips for upper body push-pull. Works well in supersets with horizontal push.
sources: Youdas, J. et al. (2010). Surface electromyographic activation patterns and elbow joint motion during a pull-up, chin-up, or perfect-pullup rotational exercise. J Strength Cond Res.
Hewit, J. et al. (2018). A comparison of muscle activation during the pull-up and three alternative pulling exercises. J Phys Fit Treatment & Sports.

exercises.name: Chin-up

difficulty.raw: Intermediate (slightly easier than pull-up due to biceps leverage)

equipment.raw: Pull-up bar. *Swaps*: assisted chin-up (band/machine) · neutral grip pull-up · supinated Cluster 3 #54 Lat Pulldown

form_cues: Same hang and pull mechanics as pull-up
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with horizontal pushing. Pairs with triceps work as upper-body push-pull. Pairs as biceps-dominant variant of vertical pull.
sources: Youdas, J. et al. (2010). Surface electromyographic activation patterns and elbow joint motion during a pull-up, chin-up, or perfect-pullup rotational exercise. J Strength Cond Res.
Doma, K. et al. (2013). The reliability of chin-ups as a measure of upper body strength. J Strength Cond Res.

exercises.name: Weighted Pull-up

equipment.raw: Pull-up bar, dip belt + plates or weighted vest. *Swaps*: weighted chin-up · Cluster 3 #54 Lat Pulldown (heavier load) · band-resisted pull-up

form_cues: Attach load via dip belt or vest
common_errors: Adding weight before bodyweight form is solid
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with weighted dip as upper-body strength duo. Pairs with rowing. Poor as fatigue accumulator (form degrades).
sources: Sanchez-Moreno, M. et al. (2017). Movement velocity as a measure of exercise intensity in pull-ups. Eur J Sport Sci.
López-Rivera, E., González-Badillo, J. (2019). Comparison of the effects of three hangboard strength and endurance training programs on grip endurance in sport climbers. J Hum Kinet.

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry

equipment.raw: Heavy dumbbells, kettlebells, or specialty trap-handles. *Swaps*: suitcase carry (single-side) · trap bar carry · kettlebell carry

form_cues: Stand tall, ribcage stacked over hips
common_errors: Loading too heavy too fast (grip fails before legs)
exercises.pairing_logic: Excellent finisher. Pairs with grip work. Pairs with core anti-rotation. Works in many conditioning circuits.
sources: McGill, S. et al. (2012). Loaded carries: development and use in performance and rehabilitation. J Athl Train (review).
McGill, S. Low Back Disorders: Evidence-Based Prevention and Rehabilitation (3rd ed., Human Kinetics, 2015).

exercises.name: Hip Thrust

equipment.raw: Barbell, plates, bench, hip pad. *Swaps*: dumbbell hip thrust · single-leg hip thrust · machine hip thrust · glute bridge (floor)

form_cues: Upper back on bench, mid-shoulder-blade contact
Squeeze glutes at top, brief pause
common_errors: Bar drifting up the body across the set
exercises.pairing_logic: Excellent paired with quad-dominant work (squat, lunge). Pairs with RDL as posterior chain duo. Layer 1 staple in supersets.
sources: Contreras, B. et al. (2015). A comparison of gluteus maximus, biceps femoris, and vastus lateralis EMG activity in the back squat and barbell hip thrust. J Appl Biomech.
Contreras, B. et al. (2017). Effects of a six-week hip thrust vs. front squat resistance training program on performance in adolescent males. J Strength Cond Res.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust

equipment.raw: Bench, optional dumbbell on hip. *Swaps*: hip thrust (bilateral) · single-leg glute bridge · cable single-leg pull-through

form_cues: Same upper-back contact as bilateral hip thrust
Lift one leg off floor, drive through working heel
Keep hips level (don't drop on free side)
common_errors: Hip dropping on non-working side (rotation compensation)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs in supersets with single-leg quad work. Excellent for asymmetry correction. Less ideal as primary lift — use bilateral for heaviest stimulus.
sources: Contreras, B. et al. (2015). A comparison of gluteus maximus, biceps femoris, and vastus lateralis EMG activity. J Appl Biomech.
Boren, K. et al. (2011). Electromyographic analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises. Int J Sports Phys Ther.

exercises.name: Single-Leg RDL

equipment.raw: Dumbbell or kettlebell. *Swaps*: B-stance RDL · regular RDL · cable single-leg pull-through · landmine single-leg RDL

form_cues: Hinge at hip, raise opposite leg behind as counterweight
Lower until hamstring stretch, weight close to leg
Drive through standing heel to return
common_errors: Bending the supporting knee too much (becomes single-leg squat)
Rounding lower back at the bottom
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs in supersets with single-leg quad work. Excellent for hamstring asymmetry. Demanding on stability — keep moderate volume.
sources: Diamant, W. et al. (2021). Single-leg vs. double-leg deadlift: a comparison of strength symmetry and lower extremity activation. J Sports Sci Med.
McAllister, M. et al. (2014). Muscle activation during various hamstring exercises. J Strength Cond Res.

exercises.name: Good Morning

equipment.raw: Barbell, plates, rack. *Swaps*: cable pull-through · seated good morning · banded good morning · RDL

form_cues: Bar on upper back, like high-bar squat
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs as primary hamstring stimulus on quad-dominant days. Poor pair with heavy deadlift same session (low-back overlap).
sources: McAllister, M. et al. (2014). Muscle activation during various hamstring exercises. J Strength Cond Res.
Hatfield, F. Powerlifting: A Scientific Approach (Contemporary Books, 1981).

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through

equipment.raw: Cable machine, rope attachment. *Swaps*: kettlebell swing · banded pull-through · RDL · hip thrust

form_cues: Face away from cable, rope between legs
Drive hips forward, squeeze glutes at top
common_errors: Using lower back to extend at top instead of glutes
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with quad-dominant work. Excellent low-back-friendly hinge alternative when deadlift volume is high.
sources: Andersen, V. et al. (2018). Resistance training with the kettlebell: a comparison of biomechanical demands of swings, snatches, and pull-throughs. J Strength Cond Res.
Schoenfeld, B. Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy (Human Kinetics, 2nd ed. 2020).

exercises.name: Glute Bridge

equipment.raw: Bodyweight or barbell, dumbbell, plate. *Swaps*: hip thrust (more ROM) · single-leg glute bridge · banded glute bridge · frog pump

form_cues: Lying flat, knees bent, feet flat
Squeeze glutes at top, ribs down
common_errors: Letting knees fall in or out
exercises.pairing_logic: Excellent activation work pre-strength. Pairs as accessory after compound hip work. Frequently used in rehab and warm-up.
sources: Boren, K. et al. (2011). Electromyographic analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises. Int J Sports Phys Ther.
Contreras, B. et al. (2015). EMG comparison of bridge variations. Strength Cond J.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat

equipment.raw: Bench, dumbbells or barbell. *Swaps*: split squat (no elevation) · walking lunge · reverse lunge · step-up

form_cues: Rear foot on bench, instep down
Front foot far enough forward (knee tracks over mid-foot)
Drive through full foot to stand
common_errors: Front foot too close (knee passes far over toe)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with hinge-dominant work or upper body. Layer 1 staple in B-supersets. Excellent for asymmetry. Pairs less well after heavy back squat (quad overload).
sources: McCurdy, K. et al. (2018). Comparison of lower extremity EMG between the 2-leg squat and modified single-leg squat. J Strength Cond Res.
Speirs, D. et al. (2016). Unilateral vs. bilateral squat training for strength, sprints, and agility in academy rugby players. J Strength Cond Res.

exercises.name: Walking Lunge

equipment.raw: Bodyweight, dumbbells, or barbell. Open space. *Swaps*: reverse lunge · forward lunge (in place) · BSS · step-up

form_cues: Step forward into stance, knee bends to ~90°
Drive through front heel to step into next rep
common_errors: Step too short (knee shoots over toe)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with hinge work. Useful as conditioning finisher. Less ideal stacked with BSS (overlapping stimulus).
sources: Stastny, P. et al. (2015). A comparison of muscle activation during the lunge variations. J Hum Kinet.
Riemann, B. et al. (2012). Comparison of biomechanical characteristics between forward and reverse lunge. Sports Biomech.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge

equipment.raw: Bodyweight, dumbbells, or barbell. *Swaps*: walking lunge · forward lunge · split squat · BSS

form_cues: Front foot stays planted, knee tracks over mid-foot
Back knee approaches floor with control
Drive through front heel to return to standing
common_errors: Step too short or too long
Pushing off back foot to assist
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs as quad-dominant accessory with upper body or hip-dominant work. Often gentler on knees than forward lunge — useful in rehab.
sources: Riemann, B. et al. (2012). Comparison of forward and reverse lunge biomechanics. J Strength Cond Res.
Stastny, P. et al. (2015). A comparison of muscle activation during the lunge variations. J Hum Kinet.

exercises.name: Step-Up

equipment.raw: Box or bench (knee-height), optional dumbbells/barbell. *Swaps*: BSS · reverse lunge · single-leg press · split squat

form_cues: Place full foot on box (not just toe)
Drive through heel of working leg
Don't push off ground with back foot
Stand fully on top, control descent
Box height: knee at ~90° at start
common_errors: Pushing off the trailing leg (loses unilateral emphasis)
exercises.pairing_logic: Excellent rehab and beginner unilateral. Pairs with hip-dominant work or upper body. Foundational functional choice.
sources: Reiman, M. et al. (2012). Hip muscle EMG during 12 hip-strengthening exercises. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther.
Boren, K. et al. (2011). Electromyographic analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises. Int J Sports Phys Ther.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat

equipment.raw: Dumbbell or kettlebell. *Swaps*: front squat · back squat · zercher squat

form_cues: Hold weight at chest, elbows tucked
Keep chest up, weight close to body
exercises.pairing_logic: Excellent for warm-up, technique work, and lighter accessory volume. Pairs with most accessories. Critical regression for Reactivator and post-rehab populations.
sources: McKean, M. et al. (2010). Knee behaviour in squatting. J Strength Cond Res.
Schoenfeld, B. (2010). Squatting kinematics and kinetics. J Strength Cond Res.

exercises.name: Nordic Hamstring Curl

equipment.raw: Anchored feet (partner, loaded barbell, GHR pad, or specialty device). *Swaps*: razor curl · GHR · stability ball leg curl · partner-assisted Nordic

form_cues: Anchor feet (heels under pads or held)
Lower under control as far as eccentric strength allows
Catch with hands at end of ROM, push back to start
common_errors: Hinging at hips (not maintaining straight body)
Falling at end of ROM uncontrolled
Going too deep too soon (injury cluster)
Using arms to push too early
exercises.pairing_logic: Excellent injury-prevention tool, particularly for runners and field-sport athletes. Demanding — moderate volume (3 sets × 5–10 reps, 1–2×/week). Soreness often substantial first weeks.
sources: Petersen, J. et al. (2011). Preventive effect of eccentric training on acute hamstring injuries in men's soccer: a cluster-randomized controlled trial. Am J Sports Med.

van Dyk, N. et al. (2019). Including the Nordic hamstring exercise in injury prevention programmes halves the rate of hamstring injuries: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 8459 athletes. Br J Sports Med.

exercises.name: Dip

equipment.raw: Parallel bars or dip station. Optional dip belt for loading. *Swaps*: bench dip · machine assisted dip · ring dip · close-grip bench press

form_cues: Slight forward lean for chest emphasis (more upright = triceps emphasis)
Lower until upper arm parallel to floor
Don't let shoulders shrug at bottom
common_errors: Going below 90° elbow (excess shoulder stress for many)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs excellently with pull-ups for upper-body push-pull. Pairs with rowing. Heavy dips poor stacked with heavy bench (overlapping pec/triceps load).
sources: McKenzie, A. et al. (2022). Differences in triceps brachii muscle activity between varying dip techniques. J Hum Kinet.
Schoenfeld, B. Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy (Human Kinetics, 2nd ed. 2020).

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press

equipment.raw: Dumbbells, bench. *Swaps*: barbell bench press · machine chest press · push-up · floor press dumbbell

form_cues: Set up like barbell bench (planted feet, retracted scapulae)
Lower with control, dumbbells trace slight arc
Press back to start, dumbbells nearly touching
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with rowing variants. Pairs with arm/shoulder isolation. Often used when barbell unavailable or for hypertrophy variation. Greater stretch at bottom than barbell variant.
sources: Saeterbakken, A. et al. (2011). The effects of bench press variations in competitive athletes on muscle activity and performance. J Hum Kinet.
Welsch, E. et al. (2005). EMG analysis of pectoralis major and anterior deltoid during the dumbbell bench press. J Strength Cond Res.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press

equipment.raw: Dumbbells, bench (seated) or no bench (standing). *Swaps*: barbell overhead press · machine shoulder press · landmine press · single-arm DB press

form_cues: Dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward (or neutral grip)
Press straight up, dumbbells nearly touch at top
Don't lock out so hard the shoulders shrug
common_errors: Pressing dumbbells out wide (loses pressing stimulus)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with rowing/pulling. Pairs with arm work. Pairs less well after heavy bench (shoulder fatigue). Accessible vertical-press variant when barbell overhead is contraindicated.
sources: Saeterbakken, A., Fimland, M. (2013). Effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses. J Strength Cond Res.
Lauver, J. et al. (2017). Influence of bench angle on upper extremity muscular activation. Eur J Sport Sci.

exercises.name: Push-Up

equipment.raw: Bodyweight (optional weight vest or band). *Swaps*: knee push-up (scaling) · incline push-up (scaling) · decline push-up (advanced) · diamond push-up · weighted push-up

form_cues: Body in straight line, head to heels
Lower with control, chest near floor
Drive through palms back to start
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with rowing or pulling. Excellent finisher or warm-up. Used heavily in rehab progressions. Endless progression versions.
sources: Calatayud, J. et al. (2014). Bench press and push-up at comparable levels of muscle activity result in similar strength gains. J Strength Cond Res.
Cogley, R. et al. (2005). Comparison of muscle activation using various hand positions during the push-up exercise. J Strength Cond Res.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row (One-Arm)

equipment.raw: Dumbbell, bench. *Swaps*: chest-supported row · Cluster 3 #55 Cable Row · barbell row · landmine row

exercises.secondary_muscles: Biceps · Posterior deltoid · Core (anti-rotation) · Erector spinae
form_cues: Knee and hand on bench, opposite leg planted
Pull dumbbell to hip, elbow tucked
Control descent, full stretch at bottom
common_errors: Twisting torso to lift heavier (cheats lats)
Pulling with arm only (no scapular movement)
exercises.pairing_logic: Layer 1 staple in Upper Push/Pull supersets. Excellent for asymmetry and core engagement. Pairs with horizontal push.
sources: Fenwick, C. et al. (2009). Comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load, and stiffness. J Strength Cond Res.
Lehman, G. et al. (2004). The importance of normalisation in the interpretation of surface electromyography. J Manipulative Physiol Ther.

exercises.name: Inverted Row

difficulty.raw: Beginner (progresses to advanced via body angle)

equipment.raw: Bar in rack at hip-to-chest height, gymnastic rings, or TRX. *Swaps*: ring row · TRX row · Cluster 3 #55 Cable Row · chest-supported row

form_cues: Body straight from head to heels (or knees if scaled)
Pull chest toward bar, elbows tucked
common_errors: Using legs to push off floor
exercises.pairing_logic: Excellent pull-up progression. Pairs with push-ups for bodyweight upper-body work. Adjust difficulty by body angle (more horizontal = harder).
sources: Youdas, J. et al. (2010). Surface electromyographic activation patterns during a pull-up, chin-up, or perfect-pullup exercise. J Strength Cond Res.
Snarr, R., Esco, M. (2014). EMG comparison of the inverted row and bodyweight row. J Strength Cond Res.

exercises.name: Face Pull

equipment.raw: Cable machine, rope attachment (or band). *Swaps*: band pull-apart · prone Y-T-W · reverse fly · band face pull

exercises.primary_muscles: Posterior deltoid · Mid-trapezius · Rhomboids · External rotators
form_cues: Cable at face height, rope grip with thumbs back
Pull rope to face, separating hands at end (external rotation)
common_errors: Going too heavy (loses form, becomes shrug or row)
exercises.pairing_logic: Universal addition to any pressing day. Pairs with bench press as antagonist. High-frequency tolerable (3–5×/week often).
sources: Cools, A. et al. (2014). Rehabilitation of scapular dyskinesis: from the office worker to the elite overhead athlete. Br J Sports Med.
Reinold, M. et al. (2009). Current concepts in the scientific and clinical rationale behind exercises for glenohumeral and scapulothoracic musculature. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise

equipment.raw: Dumbbells (or cable). *Swaps*: cable lateral raise · machine lateral raise · band lateral raise · leaning DB lateral raise

form_cues: Slight forward lean engages mid-delt better
common_errors: Leading with hands (loses lateral delt emphasis)
exercises.pairing_logic: High-frequency tolerable (delts recover quickly at this load). Pairs in supersets with pressing or pulling. Layer 1 staple in Upper P/P session.
sources: Coratella, G. et al. (2020). An electromyographic analysis of lateral raise variations and frontal raise. J Hum Kinet.
Schoenfeld, B. Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy (Human Kinetics, 2nd ed. 2020).

exercises.name: Rear Delt Fly

equipment.raw: Dumbbells, machine, or cables. *Swaps*: face pull · prone Y-T-W · band pull-apart · cable rear delt fly

form_cues: Hinge at hips OR seated bent forward
Lift weights out and back, leading with elbows
common_errors: Pulling elbows too high (becomes upright row)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with chest work as posterior balance. High-frequency suitable. Universal recommendation for desk-worker rebalancing.
sources: Cools, A. et al. (2014). Rehabilitation of scapular dyskinesis. Br J Sports Med.
Schory, A. et al. (2017). A systematic review of the exercises that produce optimal muscle ratios of the scapular stabilizers in normal shoulders. Int J Sports Phys Ther.

exercises.name: Barbell Curl

equipment.raw: Barbell or EZ-bar. *Swaps*: dumbbell curl · cable curl · EZ-bar curl · preacher curl

form_cues: Curl bar up, keeping elbows fixed
common_errors: Going too heavy (form fails, wrist strain)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with triceps work as arm-focused superset. Frequently used in arm-focused blocks. Pairs as finisher.
sources: Marcolin, G. et al. (2018). Differences in electromyographic activity between dumbbell biceps curl variations. PeerJ.
Coratella, G. et al. (2023). Biceps brachii architectural responses to incline vs. preacher curl training. J Sports Sci.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Curl

equipment.raw: Dumbbells. *Swaps*: barbell curl · cable curl · incline DB curl · concentration curl

form_cues: Standing or seated, dumbbells at sides
Curl up, supinating wrist as you go (palm faces shoulder at top)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with triceps as arm superset. Pairs as finisher. Variants (incline, concentration) target different biceps regions.
sources: Coratella, G. et al. (2023). Biceps brachii architectural responses to incline vs. preacher curl training. J Sports Sci.
Oliveira, L. et al. (2009). Effect of preacher curl seat angle on biceps brachii muscle activity. J Strength Cond Res.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl

equipment.raw: Dumbbells. *Swaps*: rope cable curl · cross-body hammer · neutral-grip curl machine

form_cues: Neutral grip throughout (palms facing each other)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with biceps curls in arm sessions. Often paired with regular curls for full-arm coverage. Excellent for forearm and brachialis development that supinated curls underdose.
sources: Marcolin, G. et al. (2018). Differences in electromyographic activity between dumbbell biceps curl variations. PeerJ.
Coratella, G. et al. (2023). Biceps brachii architectural responses. J Sports Sci.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown

equipment.raw: Cable machine, straight bar or rope or V-bar. *Swaps*: dumbbell kickback · band pushdown · diamond push-up · close-grip bench press

form_cues: Stand close to cable, slight forward lean
Control return, full stretch at top (handle near chest)
common_errors: Using torso to push down (becomes a row pattern)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with biceps curls. Frequently used as finisher. Pairs in arm-focused supersets.
sources: Maeo, S. et al. (2023). Triceps brachii hypertrophy is substantially greater after elbow extension training performed in the overhead vs. neutral arm position. Eur J Sport Sci.
Boeckh-Behrens, W., Buskies, W. Fitness-Krafttraining (Rowohlt, 2002).

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension

equipment.raw: Dumbbell, EZ-bar, or cable + rope. *Swaps*: skull crusher · cable overhead extension · single-arm DB overhead extension

form_cues: Brace core, don't arch lower back
common_errors: Going too heavy for stretch position
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with biceps work. Frequently used after pressing. Long-head stretch makes this important for full triceps development per Maeo (2023).
sources: Maeo, S. et al. (2023). Triceps brachii hypertrophy is substantially greater after elbow extension training performed in the overhead vs. neutral arm position. Eur J Sport Sci.
Kassiano, W. et al. (2022). Does varying resistance exercises promote superior muscle hypertrophy and strength gains? J Strength Cond Res.

exercises.name: Skull Crusher

equipment.raw: EZ-bar or dumbbells, bench. *Swaps*: overhead tricep extension · cable overhead extension · close-grip bench press · diamond push-up

form_cues: Lying on bench, arms vertical at start
Lower bar/dumbbells toward forehead by bending elbows
Elbows stay pointing up, shoulders fixed
Don't lock elbows so hard at top
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with biceps in arm sessions. Pairs as finisher after pressing. Often paired with overhead extension for full triceps coverage.
sources: Maeo, S. et al. (2023). Triceps brachii hypertrophy. Eur J Sport Sci.
Boehler, B. (2011). EMG analysis of the triceps brachii muscle during a variety of elbow extension exercises. UW-La Crosse Journal of Undergraduate Research.

exercises.name: Plank

equipment.raw: Bodyweight (or weighted vest for progression). *Swaps*: forearm plank · high plank · hard-style plank · long-lever plank

form_cues: Forearms on floor, elbows under shoulders
Body in straight line: head, hips, ankles
common_errors: Going too long (form deteriorates after ~60s for most)
exercises.pairing_logic: Excellent in core circuits and warm-ups. Per McGill, ~60 seconds is the upper limit before form fades; quality > duration. Frequent in rehab and prehab contexts.
sources: McGill, S. Low Back Disorders: Evidence-Based Prevention and Rehabilitation (3rd ed., Human Kinetics, 2015).
Schoenfeld, B. et al. (2014). An electromyographic comparison of a modified version of the plank with a long lever and posterior tilt versus the traditional plank exercise. Sports Biomech.

exercises.name: Side Plank

equipment.raw: Bodyweight. *Swaps*: side plank with hip dip · short-lever side plank (knees) · Copenhagen plank

form_cues: Forearm on floor, elbow under shoulder
Body in straight line, hips lifted
Top hand on hip or extended overhead
McGill recommends ~10-second reps × multiple sets vs single long hold for endurance development
exercises.pairing_logic: Layer 1 staple. Pairs with anti-rotation core work. Critical for lower-back rehab (E2) per McGill.
sources: McGill, S. Low Back Disorders: Evidence-Based Prevention and Rehabilitation (3rd ed., Human Kinetics, 2015).
McGill, S. et al. (2010). Endurance times for low back stabilization exercises. Arch Phys Med Rehabil.

exercises.name: Pallof Press

equipment.raw: Cable machine (or band). *Swaps*: band Pallof press · half-kneeling Pallof · standing Pallof · suitcase carry

form_cues: Hold handle at chest with both hands
exercises.pairing_logic: Excellent in any core circuit. Pairs in supersets with bilateral lifts. Frequent rehab choice.
sources: McGill, S. Low Back Disorders: Evidence-Based Prevention and Rehabilitation (3rd ed., Human Kinetics, 2015).
Behm, D. et al. (2010). The use of instability to train the core musculature. Appl Physiol Nutr Metab.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise

equipment.raw: Pull-up bar. *Swaps*: hanging knee raise (easier) · captain's chair leg raise · lying leg raise · ab wheel rollout

form_cues: Brace core, posteriorly tilt pelvis at start
Raise legs to ~90° (or higher with progression)
common_errors: Hip flexors dominant (no PPT, no abs)
exercises.pairing_logic: Layer 1 staple in core supersets. Pairs in Upper sessions. Demanding grip — sometimes precedes pull-up volume rather than follows.
sources: Escamilla, R. et al. (2010). Electromyographic analysis of traditional and nontraditional abdominal exercises. Phys Ther.
Vera-Garcia, F. et al. (2014). Core stability and the related strength tests in athletes. Strength Cond J.

exercises.name: Ab Roll-Out

equipment.raw: Ab wheel or barbell with plates. *Swaps*: stability ball roll-out · banded roll-out · plank · TRX fallout

form_cues: Pull back to start using core (not arms)
common_errors: Going too far before capacity allows
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with most strength work. Excellent end-of-session core. Pairs poorly with heavy deadlift same session (low-back fatigue overlap).
sources: Escamilla, R. et al. (2006). Electromyographic analysis of traditional and nontraditional abdominal exercises. Phys Ther.
McGill, S. Low Back Disorders: Evidence-Based Prevention and Rehabilitation (3rd ed., Human Kinetics, 2015).

exercises.name: Dead Bug

equipment.raw: Bodyweight (mat). *Swaps*: dead bug with band · dead bug with weight · bird-dog · supine 90/90 hold

form_cues: Lying on back, arms up, knees at 90°
Lower opposite arm and leg slowly
Lower back stays pressed to floor
exercises.pairing_logic: Excellent warm-up or rehab piece. Pairs with most activation work. Frequently used in postpartum and low-back rehab.
sources: McGill, S. Low Back Disorders: Evidence-Based Prevention and Rehabilitation (3rd ed., Human Kinetics, 2015).
Vera-Garcia, F. et al. (2007). Effects of different levels of torso coactivation on trunk muscular and kinematic responses. Clin Biomech.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown

equipment.raw: Cable machine with lat pulldown attachment (typically wide bar, sometimes V-handle or neutral-grip bar). *Swaps*: assisted pull-up · band-assisted pull-up · machine-assisted pull-up · inverted row (for very deconditioned users)

form_cues: - Sit tall, thighs locked under pads
- Grip slightly wider than shoulders (or per protocol)
- Pull elbows down and back, bar to upper chest
- Squeeze shoulder blades briefly at bottom
- Control return, full stretch at top without losing shoulder engagement
common_errors: - Leaning back excessively to use bodyweight as counterweight (bar pulls to belly, not chest)
- Pulling with arms only — no scapular movement
- Bar to back of neck (shoulder strain, no extra benefit)
- Half ROM at top (arms not fully extended)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with horizontal push (bench, DB bench, push-up). Pairs with arm work in supersets. Primary scaling option when pull-up capacity is below 5 clean reps. Lower skill floor than free-weight vertical pulls — accessible from session 1 for Reactivators and seniors.
sources: Doma, K. et al. (2013). The reliability of chin-ups and lat pulldowns as measures of upper body strength. J Strength Cond Res.
Lusk, S. et al. (2010). Grip width and forearm orientation effects on muscle activity during the lat pull-down. J Strength Cond Res.
Andersen, V. et al. (2014). Electromyographic comparison of barbell deadlift, hex bar deadlift, and hip thrust exercises (lat involvement context). J Strength Cond Res.

exercises.name: Cable Row (Seated)

equipment.raw: Cable row machine with foot platform, V-handle or wide bar attachment. *Swaps*: chest-supported row · dumbbell row · machine row · TRX row

form_cues: - Sit tall, feet planted on platform, slight knee bend
- Maintain neutral spine — no excessive forward lean at start
- Pull handle to lower ribs, elbows tucked
- Control return, full reach forward without losing core engagement
common_errors: - Rocking torso back and forth for momentum (becomes a deadlift-row hybrid)
- Pulling handle to belly button instead of lower ribs
- Lower-back rounding on the eccentric return
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with horizontal push (bench press, push-up, chest press machine). Pairs with vertical pull in upper-body sessions. Critical option for E2 Lower back rehab Phase 2 — provides horizontal pull stimulus without the spinal loading of bent-over barbell row.
sources: Fenwick, C. et al. (2009). Comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load, and stiffness. J Strength Cond Res.
Lehman, G. et al. (2004). The importance of normalisation in the interpretation of surface electromyography. J Manipulative Physiol Ther.
Schoenfeld, B. Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy (Human Kinetics, 2nd ed. 2020).

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.unilateral_note: (single-leg leg press variant on most machines)

equipment.raw: 45° leg press or horizontal leg press machine. *Swaps*: hack squat · belt squat · goblet squat · Bulgarian split squat (unilateral substitute)

substitution_alternatives.name: Cluster 1 #1 Back Squat (when free-weight is appropriate)

form_cues: - Feet shoulder-width, mid-platform — adjust placement per knee tracking
- Lower under control, knees track over toes
- Stop before lower back rounds off the pad (hip mobility limit, not depth target)
- Drive through full foot, do not lock knees explosively at top
- Maintain glute and hip contact with pad throughout
common_errors: - Shortened ROM (short presses, only knee-extension portion)
- Feet too low on platform (excess knee shear)
- Lower back rounding at depth (lifts off pad — common in users chasing depth they don't have)
- Loading too heavy too fast (machine forgives form, but loads add up)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with hamstring-dominant work (RDL, leg curl). Pairs with upper-body in Lower Anterior sessions. Primary compound-squat option for users with low-back contraindications, ankle/hip mobility limits, or post-rehab requiring controlled loading. NOT a replacement for back squat in trained-user strength programs — different stimulus profile (less core, less stabilizer, more pure quad/glute loading).
sources: Escamilla, R. et al. (2001). A three-dimensional biomechanical analysis of the squat during varying stance widths. Med Sci Sports Exerc.
Wilk, K. et al. (1996). A comparison of tibiofemoral joint forces and electromyographic activity during open and closed kinetic chain exercises. Am J Sports Med — leg press context for knee rehab.
da Silva, E. et al. (2008). Analysis of muscle activation during different leg press exercises at submaximum effort levels. J Strength Cond Res.

exercises.name: Hack Squat

movement_pattern.raw: Squat (machine, axial loading on shoulders, no spinal compression of free squat)

exercises.unilateral_note: (single-leg hack squat variant on some machines)

equipment.raw: Hack squat machine (sled-loaded with shoulder pads). *Swaps*: leg press · belt squat · safety bar squat · goblet squat

form_cues: - Back flat against pad, shoulders under shoulder pads
- Feet mid-platform, slightly narrower than back squat stance
- Lower under control, knees track over toes
- Hit depth (thighs parallel or below if mobility allows)
- Drive through full foot, do not lock knees hard
common_errors: - Heels lifting at depth (foot placement too low on platform)
- Lower back rounding off pad at depth
- Cutting depth (machine makes it easy to half-rep)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with hamstring-dominant work. Pairs with upper-body or core in Lower Anterior sessions. Distinct stimulus from leg press: axial-loaded (challenges core stability and posterior chain support) but spine-friendlier than back squat (no bar on spine). Good progression bridge between leg press (lowest spinal load) and free-weight back squat. Useful for A8 Senior and A1 Reactivator with low-back history.
sources: Coratella, G. et al. (2018). The electromyographic activities of trunk and lower limb muscles during flywheel-determined leg curl exercises (sled-loaded context). J Strength Cond Res.
Schoenfeld, B. (2010). Squatting kinematics and kinetics and their application to exercise performance. J Strength Cond Res.
Loturco, I. et al. (2018). Vertically and horizontally directed muscle power exercises: relationships with top-level sprint performance — sled-pattern force production context.

exercises.name: Quad Isolation (Leg Extension)

equipment.raw: Leg extension machine. *Swaps*: cable knee extension · band knee extension · sissy squat (advanced bodyweight alternative)

substitution_alternatives.name: Cluster 2 #27 Bulgarian Split Squat (compound alternative, different stimulus)

exercises.primary_muscles: Quadriceps (all four heads, rectus femoris especially)
form_cues: - Sit fully back, lower-back pressed to pad
- Pad sits across ankles, not shins
- Extend knees fully (controlled lockout) — do not snap
- Control descent — eccentric is where most of the stimulus lives
common_errors: - Swinging weight up with momentum (loses quad emphasis)
- Locking knees hard with bounce at top
- Letting hips lift off the seat
- Going too heavy too fast (knee discomfort common with aggressive loading)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with hamstring isolation (#59 Seated Leg Curl or #60 Lying Leg Curl) as antagonist superset — Layer 1 Lower Anterior Superset C staple. Pairs with core work. Foundational rehab exercise for E1 Knee Phase 1 — bilateral, low-load, controlled ROM is the prescribed entry point per APTA Clinical Practice Guideline for ACL rehab. Caveat: avoid heavy loads at long muscle length in users with active patellar tendinopathy mid-phase; use isometric holds instead until tendinopathy phase advances.
sources: Adams, D. et al. (2018). Knee Stability and Movement Coordination Impairments: Knee Ligament Sprain — APTA Clinical Practice Guideline (leg extension protocol for ACL rehab). J Orthop Sports Phys Ther.
Maeo, S. et al. (2021). Quadriceps muscle hypertrophy is greater after partial-range vs full-range knee extension training. Eur J Sport Sci.
Stensdotter, A. et al. (2003). Quadriceps activation in closed and in open kinetic chain exercise. Med Sci Sports Exerc.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl

equipment.raw: Seated leg curl machine with hip pad and ankle roller. *Swaps*: lying leg curl (Cluster 3 #60) · standing single-leg curl · stability ball leg curl

substitution_alternatives.name: Lying leg curl (Cluster 3 #60 — equivalent stimulus, slightly less stretch on biceps femoris per Maeo 2021)
Cluster 1 #7 RDL (compound alternative, different stimulus profile)

exercises.primary_muscles: Hamstrings (biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus — long-head bias due to hip-flexion position)
form_cues: - Sit fully back, hip pad locked over thighs
- Curl heels under hard, full ROM
- Control eccentric — the stretch position is where the hypertrophy stimulus is strongest (long-muscle-length training rationale, Maeo 2021 / Kassiano 2023)
common_errors: - Letting hip pad lift (hips coming up)
- Excessive load that prevents full ROM
- Allowing knees to wing outward at the bottom of the eccentric
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with quad isolation (#58 Leg Extension) as antagonist superset — Layer 1 Lower Posterior or Lower Anterior Superset C staple. Pairs with core work. Canonical hamstring isolation choice for hypertrophy goals (A2, G1, G3): the seated position lengthens the hamstring at the knee-flexion stretch, producing greater hypertrophy response than the lying variant per current evidence. For rehab use-cases (E1 Knee Phase 1), seated and lying are functionally interchangeable; use whichever is available.
sources: Maeo, S. et al. (2021). Greater hamstrings muscle hypertrophy but similar damage protection after training at long vs. short muscle lengths. Med Sci Sports Exerc.
Kassiano, W. et al. (2023). Influence of muscle length on hamstring hypertrophy responses to resistance training. Sports Med.
Schoenfeld, B. Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy (Human Kinetics, 2nd ed. 2020).

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl

equipment.raw: Lying leg curl machine (prone bench with ankle roller). *Swaps*: seated leg curl (Cluster 3 #59) · standing single-leg curl · stability ball leg curl

substitution_alternatives.name: Seated leg curl (Cluster 3 #59 — preferred for hypertrophy per Maeo 2021)

exercises.primary_muscles: Hamstrings (biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus — distributed activation, less long-head bias than seated)
exercises.secondary_muscles: Calves (light) · Glutes (very light hip extension support)
form_cues: - Lie prone, ankle roller above heel
- Hips pressed into bench (do not let hips lift during curl)
- Curl heels toward glutes, full ROM
- Control eccentric back to extended position
common_errors: - Hips lifting off bench (uses hip extension to assist — loses hamstring emphasis)
- Excessive load that prevents full ROM
- Roller positioned over calf instead of above heel
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with quad isolation (#58 Leg Extension) as antagonist superset. Pairs with core work. More widely available in commercial gyms than seated variant — when the user has access only to a lying leg curl, this is the default. For rehab use-cases (E1 Knee Phase 1), seated and lying are functionally interchangeable. For pure hypertrophy goals, the seated variant is preferred where available.
sources: Maeo, S. et al. (2021). Greater hamstrings muscle hypertrophy but similar damage protection after training at long vs. short muscle lengths. Med Sci Sports Exerc.
Kassiano, W. et al. (2023). Influence of muscle length on hamstring hypertrophy responses to resistance training. Sports Med.
McAllister, M. et al. (2014). Muscle activation during various hamstring exercises. J Strength Cond Res.

exercises.name: Chest Press Machine
exercises.unilateral_note: (most machines allow single-arm, but most users default to bilateral)

equipment.raw: Chest press machine (plate-loaded or selectorized; converging-arm or fixed-grip variants). *Swaps*: Cluster 1 #9 Bench Press · Cluster 2 #34 DB Bench Press · Cluster 2 #36 Push-Up · floor press

substitution_alternatives.name: Cluster 1 #9 Bench Press (when free-weight is appropriate + spotter available)

form_cues: - Adjust seat so handles align with mid-chest at start
- Sit tall, scapulae retracted against pad
- Press to full but not aggressive lockout
- Control return, full stretch without losing scapular position
- Feet planted, do not push through legs for momentum
common_errors: - Seat too high or too low (handles align wrong, shoulder strain pattern)
- Letting scapulae round forward at the stretch
- Pushing through the lower back (lifts from seat)
- Going too heavy too fast (machine forgives form, loads accumulate quickly)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with horizontal pull (Cable Row #55, DB Row, Pull-up). Pairs with arm/shoulder isolation. Primary horizontal push option for A1 Reactivator early phases (no spotter required), A6 Postpartum (controlled return to pressing patterns post-clearance), A8 Senior (lower stabilizer demand). NOT a substitute for bench press in trained-user strength programs — different stabilizer profile, less transferable to athletic patterns.
sources: Saeterbakken, A. et al. (2011). The effects of bench press variations in competitive athletes on muscle activity and performance. J Hum Kinet.
Welsch, E. et al. (2005). EMG analysis of pectoralis major and anterior deltoid during the dumbbell bench press. J Strength Cond Res.
Schick, E. et al. (2010). A comparison of muscle activation between a Smith machine and free weight bench press. J Strength Cond Res — fixed-path vs free-weight stabilizer comparison.

exercises.name: Shoulder Press Machine

equipment.raw: Shoulder press machine (plate-loaded or selectorized; converging or fixed-grip variants). *Swaps*: Cluster 1 #12 Overhead Press · Cluster 2 #35 DB Shoulder Press · landmine press · seated dumbbell press

substitution_alternatives.name: Cluster 1 #12 Overhead Press (when free-weight standing is appropriate)
Cluster 2 #34 DB Bench Press incline (alternative angle when overhead is contraindicated)

exercises.secondary_muscles: Upper pectoralis · (minimal core — seated machine removes anti-extension demand)
form_cues: - Adjust seat so handles align with shoulders at start
- Sit tall, back pressed against pad
- Press to full but not aggressive lockout (do not shrug shoulders into pads)
- Control return, handles to shoulder height
- Brace core, do not push through the lower back
common_errors: - Seat too low (handles start too high, shoulder strain at lockout)
- Letting shoulders shrug toward ears at lockout
- Half ROM (partial press, especially at the stretch)
- Driving hips forward to assist (defeats machine support)
exercises.pairing_logic: Pairs with vertical pull (Lat Pulldown #54, Pull-up). Pairs with arm work. Primary vertical-press option for A1 Reactivator early phases, A6 Postpartum (controlled overhead reintroduction post-clearance), A8 Senior (back-supported reduces core anti-extension demand), E3 Shoulder rehab Phase 3 (controlled overhead reintroduction per protocol). Not a substitute for standing overhead press in trained-user programs — different core and stabilizer profile.
sources: Saeterbakken, A., Fimland, M. (2013). Effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses. J Strength Cond Res.
Lauver, J. et al. (2017). Influence of bench angle on upper extremity muscular activation during bench press exercise. Eur J Sport Sci.
Cools, A. et al. (2014). Rehabilitation of scapular dyskinesis: from the office worker to the elite overhead athlete (shoulder press progression context). Br J Sports Med.
